subject.title: fix(status): use legacy Codex OAuth profiles for OpenAI usage

question: Should provider-usage runtime accept retired `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles for canonical `openai` status usage before doctor migration, or require users to run `openclaw doctor --fix` first?
rationale: Repository policy makes legacy OpenAI-Codex ids doctor-owned by default, but the PR proof shows a real upgrade case where status usage is missing until that migration runs; automation should not choose that compatibility exception for maintainers.

options.title: Approve scoped usage bridge
options.body: Accept the runtime fallback only for provider-usage OAuth/token status paths, keep API keys excluded, and require the branch to resolve conflicts against current main.

options.title: Keep doctor-only migration
options.body: Reject the runtime fallback and ask affected users to run `openclaw doctor --fix` before status usage reads legacy profile state.

options.title: Narrow before deciding
options.body: Require a revised patch that documents the removal boundary and proves it cannot overlap with the merged Codex synthetic app-server route.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped usage bridge
recommendation.body: Accept the runtime fallback only for provider-usage OAuth/token status paths, keep API keys excluded, and require the branch to resolve conflicts against current main.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the OpenAI provider identity unification and legacy-state migration boundary that this PR would intentionally soften.
